skill.name: managing-commits
skill.description: Create, review, and organize Git commits using Conventional Commits, git history analysis, and optional GitHub issue references from a local cache.
skill.summary: Generate and review Conventional Commits with Git history and GitHub issue context.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command alerts are false positives from documented Git commands or subprocess calls that pass argument lists without shell execution. Confirmed risks are limited to an unsafe fixed temporary commit-message file and persistent caching of GitHub issue metadata. No evidence found for prompt injection or hidden data-exfiltration instructions in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Replace /tmp/commit-msg.txt with a secure tempfile created with restrictive permissions, and delete it after git reads it.
Document the cache path, minimize stored issue body text, and ensure .claude/github-workflows is ignored by version control.
Require explicit user confirmation before commit, rebase, squash, or history rewrite commands, and show the exact planned command.

content.user_title: Manage Git Commits with Conventional Workflows
content.value_statement: Poor commit messages make history hard to review and automate. This skill helps generate, validate, group, and review Conventional Commits with GitHub issue context.
actual_capabilities: Generate Conventional Commit messages from staged or changed files.
Validate commit subjects, bodies, footers, and issue references.
Analyze recent commit history for unclear, large, or nonstandard commits.
Group changed files into logical commit sets by scope and type.
Suggest GitHub issue references from branch names and cached issue data.
limitations: Requires a Git repository for history and diff analysis.
GitHub issue features require the GitHub CLI and authentication.
Automated grouping is heuristic and needs user review before committing.
The helper scripts can write local cache files under .claude.

use_cases.title: Create Feature Commits
use_cases.description: Turn staged feature work into a clear Conventional Commit with scope, body, and issue footer.

use_cases.title: Review Branch History
use_cases.description: Find unclear, oversized, or nonstandard commits before opening or merging a pull request.

use_cases.title: Plan Multi-Commit Changes
use_cases.description: Group a mixed working tree into separate feature, test, documentation, and fix commits.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Commit Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me write a Conventional Commit message for my staged changes. Show the suggested subject, body, and footer before any commit.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Recent Commits
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my last five commits for Conventional Commit format, clarity, issue references, and commit size. Suggest exact improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Group a Mixed Change Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze all changed files and propose logical commit groups by type and scope. Include file lists and commit messages for each group.

prompt_templates.title: Repair Branch History
prompt_templates.prompt: Review commits on this branch against main and create a reword or squash plan. Ask before running any history-changing command.

output_examples.input: Help me commit my staged authentication changes.
output_examples.output: Suggested commit: feat(auth): add JWT token refresh. The body explains the refresh behavior, and the footer closes the related issue.

output_examples.input: Review my branch commits before the pull request.
output_examples.output: The review identifies two clear commits, one vague work-in-progress commit, and one large commit that should be split.

output_examples.input: Commit all current changes, but split them cleanly.
output_examples.output: The plan separates implementation, tests, documentation, and a small API fix into distinct Conventional Commits.

best_practices: Review the proposed commit plan before allowing any commit command.
Keep each commit focused on one logical change.
Use issue-closing footers only when the change fully resolves the issue.
anti_patterns: Do not combine feature, test, documentation, and refactor work in one unclear commit.
Do not accept generated issue references without checking the related issue.
Do not rewrite shared branch history without team approval.

faq.question: Does this skill make commits automatically?
faq.answer: It supports commit workflows, but users should confirm commands before repository changes.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub?
faq.answer: No. Basic commit generation works with Git. Issue sync requires the GitHub CLI and authentication.

faq.question: Can it split a large change into several commits?
faq.answer: Yes. It can group changed files by scope, type, and relationship, then propose separate commits.

faq.question: Can it validate existing commits?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review recent commits or branch commits for format, clarity, and size.

faq.question: Where does issue data get stored?
faq.answer: The helper scripts store issue cache files under .claude/github-workflows in the project.

faq.question: Can it handle breaking changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can include breaking change markers and footer text when a change requires migration notes.
